evidence_summary: Tonehome documents the EKO Multitone as an Italian pedal and cites the 1973 EKO catalogue. Secondary historical discussion notes similarities to UK and Japanese designs, but similarity is not sufficient to establish an external builder. Retain EKO as marketed identity with builder unconfirmed until model-specific production evidence is found.

A secondary source proposes that the Multitone may incorporate a Japanese fuzz lineage, but the evidence presented does not establish a Japanese-made fuzz section or a specific supplier. Do not publish as manufacturing fact.

Schaller is documented as the West German manufacturer of its own vintage fuzz and as the source for multiple OEM-marketed identities. Effects Database and vintage Hofner documentation independently support the Schaller/Hofner relationship.

Vintage Hofner documentation says Hofner's early fuzz pedals were also available with Schaller markings, supporting Schaller manufacture; Effects Database specifically identifies No. 539 as a Schaller OEM pedal.
Effects Database documents the Hofner Wha-Wha-Fuzz as a German-made unit produced by Schaller and related to Schaller's own Wha-Wha-Fuzz.
Schaller Fuzz-Sustain is documented as Schaller-manufactured and sold under related Höfner and Allsound identities. Keep each marketed identity separate from the physical builder record.
Effects Database documents the rare dual-treadle Schaller Double Pedal as produced in Germany in the late 1960s and notes a Höfner-branded equivalent.
